findings.title: Login-cache test never deletes the IdPs it creates
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup with testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove (also at line 425) instead of the alias just created (idp-alias-N). Cleanup therefore DELETEs a non-existent provider named "alias" and leaves every broker this test created in the shared realm. Those include enabled, non-hidden login IdPs, so a later run of this test (or any other test that counts getForLogin results) sees extra providers and the hard-coded sizes (5, 6, 10, 11) no longer match. If an IdP literally aliased "alias" exists, cleanup deletes that one instead.

findings.title: Cached getForLogin drops query order
findings.body: getForLogin collects delegate ids into a Set and then copies the resolved models into a HashSet before returning identityProviders.stream(). The previous uncached implementation returned the delegate stream, which is ordered (typically guiOrder / alias) for the login page. HashSet iteration order is undefined and not stable, and the order is not stored in IdentityProviderListQuery, so it cannot be reconstructed on a cache hit. Callers that do not re-sort will show identity-provider buttons in a different order on every request; only OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean sorts after the call.

findings.title: Login cache can return IdPs that are no longer eligible
findings.body: On a cache hit, each stored id is loaded with getById and added unconditionally. Nothing re-applies LoginFilter (enabled, not link-only, not hide-on-login, public org broker) and nothing drops a model whose organization-aware isEnabled() is now false. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate also skips invalidation when both the wrapped original and the update still pass the login predicate and the organization id is unchanged, and organization enable/disable never touches the .idp.login keys. After an org is disabled, or after an eligibility change that the short-circuit misses, getForLogin keeps returning that broker until some unrelated login IdP is created, updated, or removed. The contract is that results are suitable for the login page; only two branches of OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean re-check isEnabled(), so every other caller keeps showing those providers.

findings.title: Login predicate NPEs when config map is null
findings.body: The new clause calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) whenever organizationId is non-null. getConfig() is not null-safe (setConfig(null) and some deserialized models leave it null), and Boolean.parseBoolean is only reached after the map dereference. getLoginPredicate() now runs on the create, update, and remove write path inside the cache provider. An org-linked IdP with a null config map therefore throws NullPointerException and rolls back the write instead of being treated as not public.
